title: Product
description: A product: the root of its specifications and its own space, whose records link only to each other, with the roles its use cases name, the interfaces its flows go through, the kinds and relations it declares, and its open questions.

title: Product kind
description: A kind a product adds to Lathe's, such as a report or a CLI command. Its records sit under one parent kind, and its fields are product_kind_field rows.

title: Role
description: A role the product's records name, such as Owner, Reader or Agent: a use case's actors and a question's owner. Specs name roles, never people.

title: Domain
description: A part of the product with its own model, language and owner, for one business capability: what DDD calls a bounded context. Domains meet only through published events.

title: Capability
description: An ordered slice of a domain that groups its use cases, such as Catalog or Lending.

title: Aggregate
description: The consistency boundary: a cluster of entities changed together as one unit, by one command at a time. Other aggregates follow its changes through events, and refer to it by ID only.

title: Entity field
description: One field of an entity, in order. Its table's columns follow from it.

title: Entity
description: A record the domain keeps, with an identity: its aggregate's root or one of its children. Its fields are entity_field rows; the value objects it has are the ones its fields are typed with.

title: Invariant
description: A rule that holds for one aggregate on every change. Uniqueness across records (no two members share an email) is an invariant, enforced by a unique key of the table.

title: Domain event
description: An unchangeable record that something happened to an aggregate, named in the past tense (Loan opened), raised by its commands. What it carries are event_field rows.

title: Use case
description: An actor's goal: its actors (use_case_actor rows), its UC requirements and its flows, one per interface it happens through. It changes nothing itself; its flows' steps invoke commands and queries.

title: UC requirement
description: One rule a use case must follow. Steps of the use case's own flow fulfill it.

title: Pattern
description: Behavior several use cases share, stated once with the settings each use case that follows it fills in. Its settings are pattern_setting rows and its rules pattern_rule records.

title: Pattern rule
description: One rule of a pattern. Every domain that follows the pattern owes it, unless it names a setting all of that domain's followers mark Not applicable, or its applies-when condition is met by no follower there.

title: Pattern setting
description: One setting of a pattern, in order: what each follower decides.

title: Flow
description: How its use case is carried out through one interface: the steps on its main path and its alternate paths. A use case has one flow per interface it happens through, and each flow belongs only to it.

title: Flow step
description: One step of a flow, in order on its path. It fulfills UC requirements of its own use case, invokes at most one command or query, happens in at most one view and may exchange with integrations.

title: View
description: A screen or page a person uses. It has no owner: it exists because flow steps happen in it, its product follows from its ID, and it belongs to the one domain whose flow steps happen in it, or is shared when two or more do, or none.

title: Endpoint
description: An HTTP endpoint that exposes exactly one command or query, its parent. Flow steps reach it through their command or query, never directly.

title: Open question
description: Something undecided, with the role that decides it. It sits under its product or one of its domains, and may be about any record (the about link). A decided question is removed and its answer written into the records it affects.

title: Integration
description: An outside system the product exchanges with, such as a payment provider or a mail service. It has no owner: it exists because flow steps exchange with it, its product follows from its ID, and it belongs to the one domain whose flow steps exchange with it, or is shared when two or more do, or none.

title: Product kind field
description: One typed field of a product kind, in order: a column of its table.

title: Product relation
description: A pair of kinds a product lets a relation link. A new relation name gets its own link table; a name Lathe already has adds the pair to that relation, when its link table's ends accept the two kinds.

title: Term
description: A word of the domain's glossary and what it means there, so specs, code and conversation use one language.

title: Value object
description: A value with no identity of its own, such as an email address or a money amount, defined by its fields and checked by its constraints when it is created. It has no owner: it exists because entities, events or read models use it as a field's type, its product follows from its ID, and it belongs to the one domain whose fields it types, or is shared when two or more domains use it, or none.

title: Value object field
description: One field of a value object, in order. A table flattens a value object's fields into columns.

title: Constraint
description: A value object's own rule, checked when the value is created, such as an email address having one @.

title: Specification
description: A named predicate over one or more aggregates of one domain (Evans), such as Member in good standing. Commands check it before acting, and queries may select by it. It has no owner: it reads its aggregates, and its domain follows from its ID.

title: Event field
description: One field a domain event carries, in order. A published event's fields are a contract with other domains.

title: Command
description: A request to change exactly one aggregate: the one its entity belongs to. It sits under the entity it changes, and checks specifications, raises events and may call domain services, all of its own domain.

title: Command change
description: A recorded exception to one aggregate per command: another aggregate of the same domain the command changes in the same transaction, and why. `lathe check` and the Checks page list every one under Recorded exceptions.

title: Read model
description: A view of its domain's data shaped for reading, which reads one or more of the domain's aggregates. Its fields are read_model_field rows, and it is stored in a table of its own.

title: Read model field
description: One field of a read model, in order. Its table's columns follow from it.

title: Query
description: A question asked of one read model, its parent. It changes nothing, and may select by specifications and call domain services of its own domain.

title: Policy
description: Whenever an event, then a command (event storming). It belongs to the command it invokes and hears one event: its own domain's, or another domain's published one.

title: Domain service
description: Domain logic that belongs to no single entity and is not a yes-or-no check, such as calculating a late fee. Commands and queries of its domain call it; it uses no storage and no outside system.

title: Use case actor
description: One actor of a use case, in order: a role of the use case's product.

title: View requirement
description: One rule a view must follow, such as what it shows while loading or a field's limits.

title: API requirement
description: One rule an endpoint must follow, such as an error's response or a limit on its request.

title: Repository
description: Loads and saves its aggregate, whole: the way command handlers reach the aggregate's storage. It persists exactly one aggregate, linked with persists, and sits under its domain, or, for one several domains share, under the domain that holds what they share. One that also persists other aggregates records each as a repository share, with its reason.

title: Data model
description: Its entity in code: the entity's data, behavior and mapping to its table. A command is carried out by its handler and its aggregate root's data model.

title: Table
description: Where an entity or a read model, its parent, is stored, in a database or not; or, under a domain, a table of the domain's own infrastructure that implements no design record, such as its outbox. Its columns follow from its parent's fields, a value object's fields flattened into columns, so it stores only what fields cannot say: its keys and indexes (table_key rows). An entity's table holds its rows, the source of truth: a table, normalized, or the browser storage, file or memory that keeps them; a read model's is a projection that can be rebuilt, usually a view over its domain's entity tables, or computed in memory on each load.

title: Table key
description: One key or index of a table, in order: its primary key, a unique key with the invariant it enforces, a foreign key with the table it points at, or an index. A foreign key points at a table of the same domain: a reference to another domain's aggregate stays a plain ID.

title: Value type
description: Its value object in code, which checks the value object's constraints when a value is created.

title: Predicate
description: Its specification in code: a yes-or-no test over the records it is given.

title: Event type
description: Its domain event's shape in code; a contract with other domains when the event is published.

title: Projection
description: Fills its read model's table and keeps it current, from events or as a view's query. It writes only its own read model's table.

title: Command handler
description: Carries out its command: an application service that owns the transaction, loads the aggregate through its repository, checks specifications and raises events. What clean architecture calls a use case or interactor.

title: Query handler
description: Answers its query from its read model's table: an application service that changes nothing.

title: Event handler
description: Carries out its policy: hears the policy's event and sends its command.

title: Service
description: Its domain service in code. It never uses a repository or an outside system: its inputs are passed in, and it returns a value or a decision.

title: UI component
description: A piece of the user interface that renders one or more views. It has no owner: it exists because views use it, its product follows from its ID, and it belongs to the one domain that uses the views it renders, or is shared when two or more do, or none.

title: Endpoint handler
description: Serves its endpoint: reads the request, calls the command or query handler and writes the response.

title: Adapter
description: Talks to its integration's outside system, so the rest of the code does not.

title: Standard
description: A library of engineering rules that holds for the product's code, such as logging, error handling or naming. What follows one of its rules meets it.

title: Standard rule
description: One rule of a standard. Technical records that follow it link to it with meets; its standard rule tests prove it.

title: Constraint test
description: Proves its constraint: the values its value object accepts and refuses.

title: Invariant test
description: Proves its invariant: a change that would break it is refused, and the aggregate stays as it was.

title: Specification test
description: Proves its specification: which records satisfy the predicate and which do not.

title: Policy test
description: Proves its policy: when its event happens, its command is sent.

title: Domain service test
description: Proves its domain service: from the inputs given, the value or decision it returns.

title: Use case test
description: Proves its UC requirement, at the level the use case is stated: what the actor does and what the product does in answer.

title: View test
description: Proves its view requirement in the view.

title: Endpoint test
description: Proves its API requirement at the endpoint: the request and the response.

title: Flow test
description: A smoke test of its flow's main path, end to end, at the level that fits its interface.

title: Integration test
description: Proves an exchange with its integration's outside system.

title: Pattern rule test
description: Proves its pattern rule in one domain that adopts the pattern: one test per pattern rule and adopting domain.

title: Standard rule test
description: Proves its standard rule in the product's code, such as a scan of the code for what the rule forbids: any number per rule, at any level.

title: Interface
description: A way the product is used, such as its web app, its HTTP API or its command line. A use case happens through one or more interfaces, with one flow for each, and the interface's kind says what that flow's steps go through.

title: Business outcome
description: A measurable change the product exists to bring about: its statement, measure and target, and what measures it (measured_by).

title: Extension record
description: A record of a product's own kind: an ID, a title, its one parent and the fields its kind declares, with the links it starts and the packages it uses.

title: Entry point
description: A start-up file: what runs first and wires the rest together, under the domain it starts.

title: Tooling
description: A dev script or config file outside the running product, under the domain whose code it builds, checks or tests.

title: Test data set
description: What some tests start from: the environment, the accounts and the starting records, how to prepare and reset them, and the file that builds them. Tests link to it with starts_from.

title: Rule
description: Its invariant in code: the rule in the aggregate's rules.ts that the aggregate's commands run before saving and every load runs over all data, named as its refusal names it. An invariant is built only through its rule.

title: Check
description: One rule the engine applies: a row of the `check` table whose query returns a row for each problem it finds.

title: Product setting
description: A product's `product_setting` row: the most children of one kind a record of the product should hold, and the most entities an aggregate should hold.

title: Page
description: One place in the app, identified by its address, showing a view of one loaded workspace.

title: Space
description: One product as a place to work in, in the rail.

title: Nav row
description: A row of the nav that folds, and whether the reader has it folded.

title: Tab set
description: The tabs open in one space of the desktop app, in order, with one active.

title: Tab
description: One place in the row: its focus and stage, its view, and its own history of where the Reader went in it.

title: Session settings
description: How the graph is laid out and how wide the wiki card is, for this browser session.

title: History entry
description: One place a tab went to, in its own Back and Forward history.

title: Panel
description: One part of the page's layout, which always shows the page's focus and can be hidden without losing it.

title: Keyboard command
description: Something a person can do from anywhere in the app, listed once in the keymap.

title: Key binding
description: One chord or sequence that runs the command, never shared with another command active at the same time.

title: Theme
description: One theme: a named set of token values with a light set and a dark set.

title: Product window
description: One window showing one product folder.

title: Recent folder
description: One folder the person opened lately, for File › Open Recent and the next launch.

title: App server
description: What one window loads Lathe from.

title: Appearance
description: The person's appearance: the theme in use and the color mode.

title: Recent folders
description: The list of recent folders, one per shell.

title: Product repo
description: A product repo: its root folder, the schema version its data is for, where its data files are, and the other products it shows as a workspace.

title: Pattern following
description: A domain or use case that follows one pattern.

title: Setting value
description: A `setting_value` row: the value a following use case, or a domain that follows the pattern itself, gives one of the pattern's settings.
